name: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
description: Official legislation grounded in the statutory corpus.

sections.title: Section 1
sections.content: Short title, extent, commencement and application. (1) This Act may be called the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. (2) It extends to the whole of India. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint.

sections.title: Section 2
sections.content: Section 2(1): 'advertisement' means any audio or visual publicity, representation, endorsement or pronouncement made by means of light, sound, smoke, gas, print, electronic media, internet or website.

sections.title: Section 3
sections.content: Central Consumer Protection Council. (1) The Central Government shall, by notification, establish with effect from such date as it may specify in such notification, a Council to be known as the Central Consumer Protection Council. (2) The Central Council shall be an advisory council.

sections.title: Section 4
sections.content: Procedure for meetings of Central Council. The Central Council shall meet as and when necessary, but at least one meeting of the Council shall be held every year.

sections.title: Section 5
sections.content: Objects of Central Council. The objects of the Central Council shall be to promote and protect the rights of the consumers under this Act.

sections.title: Section 6
sections.content: State Consumer Protection Councils. (1) Every State Government shall, by notification, establish with effect from such date as it may specify in such notification, a State Consumer Protection Council for such State.

sections.title: Section 7
sections.content: Procedure for meetings of State Council. The State Council shall meet as and when necessary, but not less than two meetings shall be held every year.

sections.title: Section 8
sections.content: Objects of State Council. The objects of every State Council shall be to promote and protect within the State the rights of the consumers.

sections.title: Section 9
sections.content: District Consumer Protection Council. (1) The State Government shall, by notification, establish for every district a District Consumer Protection Council to be known as the District Council.

sections.title: Section 10
sections.content: Establishment of Central Consumer Protection Authority. (1) The Central Government shall, by notification, establish a Central Authority to be known as the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers.

sections.title: Section 11
sections.content: Qualifications, terms of office of Chief Commissioner and Commissioners. The Central Government may, by notification, make rules relating to qualifications, appointment, term of office, salaries and allowances of Chief Commissioner and Commissioners.

sections.title: Section 12
sections.content: Vacancy, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of Central Authority. No act or proceeding of the Central Authority shall be invalid merely by reason of any vacancy in or defect in constitution.

sections.title: Section 13
sections.content: Appointment of officers, experts, professionals and administrative staff of Central Authority. The Central Government shall provide the Central Authority with such officers and other employees as it considers necessary.

sections.title: Section 14
sections.content: Procedure of Central Authority. The Central Authority shall regulate the procedure for transaction of its business and allocation of business among Chief Commissioner and Commissioners.

sections.title: Section 15
sections.content: Investigation Wing. (1) The Central Authority shall have an Investigation Wing headed by a Director-General for the purpose of conducting inquiry or investigation under this Act.

sections.title: Section 16
sections.content: Power of District Collector. The District Collector may, on a complaint or reference made to him or taken suo motu, inquire into or investigate complaints regarding violation of rights of consumers.

sections.title: Section 17
sections.content: Complaints to Authorities. A complaint relating to violation of consumer rights or unfair trade practices or false or misleading advertisements may be made in writing or in electronic form to the District Collector, Regional Director, or Central Authority.

sections.title: Section 18
sections.content: Powers and functions of Central Authority. (1) The Central Authority shall protect, promote and enforce the rights of consumers as a class, prevent unfair trade practices, and ensure no false or misleading advertisements are made.

sections.title: Section 19
sections.content: Power of Central Authority to refer matter for investigation or recall goods. (1) The Central Authority may, after receiving information or on suo motu action, direct Director-General or District Collector to investigate.

sections.title: Section 20
sections.content: Power of Central Authority to recall goods, etc. Where the Central Authority is satisfied that there is a prima facie case of violation of consumer rights, it may pass order for recall of goods or withdrawal of services.

sections.title: Section 21
sections.content: Power of Central Authority to issue directions and penalties against false or misleading advertisements. The Central Authority may issue directions to discontinue or modify false advertisements and impose penalties up to ten lakh rupees.

sections.title: Section 22
sections.content: Search and seizure. (1) The Director-General or any other officer authorised by him may enter, search and seize any record, document or article.

sections.title: Section 23
sections.content: Designation of any statutory authority or body to function as Central Authority. The Central Government may designate any existing statutory authority to perform functions of Central Authority.

sections.title: Section 24
sections.content: Appeal against order passed by Central Authority. Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Central Authority under section 20 or section 21 may file an appeal to the National Commission within thirty days.

sections.title: Section 25
sections.content: Grants by Central Government. The Central Government may make to the Central Authority grants of such sums of money as it thinks fit.

sections.title: Section 26
sections.content: Accounts and audit of Central Authority. (1) The Central Authority shall maintain proper accounts and other relevant records and prepare an annual statement of accounts.

sections.title: Section 27
sections.content: Annual report of Central Authority. The Central Authority shall prepare once in every year an annual report giving full account of its activities during the previous year.

sections.title: Section 28
sections.content: Establishment of District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. (1) The State Government shall, by notification, establish a District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in each district of the State.

sections.title: Section 29
sections.content: Qualifications, etc., of President and members of District Commission. The Central Government may make rules to provide for qualifications, appointment, term of office, and salaries of President and members.

sections.title: Section 30
sections.content: Salaries, allowances and other terms and conditions of service of President and members of District Commission. Terms of service of President and members shall be as prescribed by Central Government.

sections.title: Section 34
sections.content: Jurisdiction of District Commission. (1) Subject to other provisions, District Commission has jurisdiction for complaints where consideration paid does not exceed one crore rupees.

sections.title: Section 35
sections.content: Manner in which complaint shall be made. A complaint in relation to goods sold or services provided may be filed with District Commission by consumer, recognized association, or government.

sections.title: Section 39
sections.content: Findings of District Commission. (1) Where District Commission is satisfied about defects or deficiency, it shall issue order directing removal of defect, replacement, refund, or compensation.

sections.title: Section 47
sections.content: Jurisdiction of State Commission. (1) State Commission has jurisdiction for complaints where consideration exceeds rupees one crore but does not exceed rupees ten crore.

sections.title: Section 58
sections.content: Jurisdiction of National Commission. (1) National Commission has jurisdiction for complaints where consideration paid exceeds rupees ten crore.

sections.title: Section 69
sections.content: Limitation period. (1) District Commission, State Commission or National Commission shall not admit complaint unless filed within two years from cause of action.

sections.title: Section 82
sections.content: Application of product liability. Chapter VI applies to every claim for product liability made in a complaint for harm caused by defective product or deficient service.

sections.title: Section 83
sections.content: Liability of product manufacturer. Product manufacturer liable for manufacturing defect, design defect, deviation from specification, or breach of warranty.

name: Right to Information Act, 2005
description: Official legislation grounded in the statutory corpus.

sections.title: Section 1
sections.content: Short title, extent and commencement. (1) This Act may be called the Right to Information Act, 2005. (2) It extends to the whole of India. (3) Sections 4(1), 5(1), 5(2), 12, 13, 15, 16, 24, 27 and 28 shall come into force at once, and remaining provisions on 120th day of enactment.

sections.title: Section 2
sections.content: Definitions. In this Act, unless context otherwise requires, 'information' means any material in any form including records, documents, memos, e-mails, opinions, advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, contracts, reports, papers, samples, models, data held electronically.

sections.title: Section 3
sections.content: Right to information. Subject to the provisions of this Act, all citizens shall have the right to information.

sections.title: Section 4
sections.content: Obligations of public authorities. (1) Every public authority shall maintain all its records duly catalogued and indexed to facilitate right to information and ensure proactive public disclosures.

sections.title: Section 5
sections.content: Designation of Public Information Officers. Every public authority shall designate Central Public Information Officers or State Public Information Officers in all administrative units.

sections.title: Section 6
sections.content: Request for obtaining information. A person desiring information under this Act shall make a request in writing or electronically in English, Hindi, or official language of area accompanied by prescribed fee.

sections.title: Section 7
sections.content: Disposal of request. Public Information Officer shall provide information or reject request as expeditiously as possible and within thirty days of receipt of request.

sections.title: Section 8
sections.content: Exemption from disclosure of information. Exemption applies to information affecting sovereignty, security, strategic interests, cabinet papers, trade secrets, or personal privacy.

sections.title: Section 19
sections.content: Appeals. Any person not receiving decision within specified time or aggrieved by decision of CPIO or SPIO may prefer first appeal within thirty days. Second appeal lies to Information Commission within ninety days.

sections.title: Section 20
sections.content: Penalties. Information Commission may impose penalty of 250 rupees each day up to 25,000 rupees on PIO for delaying or refusing information without reasonable cause.
